approved: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 1) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would make minor corrections to four veterans' compensation laws to match the government's original policy intent.

It would give the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission power to make rules before July 2026 and preserve some treatment-related instruments under the Veterans' Entitlements Act as if they were made under the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act.
The bill also clarifies that funeral compensation claims are decided under the act they were lodged under and fixes the review path for certain determinations made before 21 April 2025.
Gives the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission pre-commencement powers to make instruments before 1 July 2026.
Keeps treatment-related instruments made under the Veterans' Entitlements Act operating as if they were made under the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act.
Confirms that funeral compensation claims are decided under the act under which they were lodged.
Clarifies the review pathway for claimants with original determinations under the DRCA made before 21 April 2025.
Veterans and their families who claim compensation or rehabilitation under the MRCA, VEA or DRCA.

Moved the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No 1) Bill 2025, arguing that minor technical amendments would support the transition from the tri-act veterans compensation system to the single Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004 from the middle of 2026, clarify review and funeral benefit provisions, and preserve transitional instruments and review rights.

Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the VET Student Loans (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2025 and Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 1) Bill 2025 stood referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Spoke in the absence of the shadow minister for veterans' affairs and indicated that the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 1) Bill 2025 should proceed, with debate adjourned.

Reported that the Federation Chamber orders for the VET Student Loans (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2025 and Veterans Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures No. 1) Bill 2025 were returned to the House for further consideration and would be considered later that day.

Supported amendments to implement the VETS Act, including transitional powers, continuity of treatment arrangements, funeral compensation rules and review rights, ahead of a single veterans entitlement framework commencing on 1 July 2026.

Moved the second reading of legislation making technical amendments to support the Veterans' Entitlements, Treatment and Support (Simplification and Harmonisation) Act 2025 and its transition to a single veterans entitlement framework from 1 July 2026, stating that existing payments and benefits would continue uninterrupted.
